title: Accounts
summary: The companies your leads belong to. An account is little more than a name: its job is to be picked in the Account Name box of a lead, and to be printed as the "Bill To" of a proposal.
text: Accounts The companies your leads belong to. An account is little more than a name: its job is to be picked in the Account Name box of a lead, and to be printed as the "Bill To" of a proposal. The list has two columns, AccountId (assigned by the database, you cannot type it) and AccountName, and the second one always stretches to fill the window. Unlike leads and proposals, accounts are not filtered by the active user: everybody sees the same list. Create Create asks for the name in a small dialog that starts out filled with New Account, then appends the row. The name is not checked: you can create two accounts with the same name, or one with an empty name, and nothing will complain. The sample data already contains one account with an empty name and id 0 — it comes with the demo, it is not something you did. Remove Remove deletes the selected row immediately, without asking. There is no undo. Nothing stops you from removing an account that leads are pointing at: the leads keep the name they had stored, and the box in their detail window will show a name that is no longer in the list. Search The Search box filters as you type, on the account name only, ignoring upper and lower case, matching anywhere in the name — typing or finds both Apollo Orange, LLC. and Vulcan Mercury Company. Clear the box to see everything again. Export Export saves the whole table — not the filtered list — to a file you choose. The format is FireDAC's own (binary, XML or JSON according to the extension you give it), which the same application can read back; it is not a spreadsheet file. For something you can open in Excel, use the export on the Marketing page, which writes a delimited text file. The navigator at the bottom The row of arrows under the list moves the selection, and the +, − and ✓ buttons insert, delete and post a row directly in the grid. They work on the same table the buttons above use, so a row inserted here is an account like any other.

title: Asking the assistant
summary: The application carries this manual inside it, and an assistant that has read it. Instead of looking a page up, you can ask — and for a few things, you can ask it to do the work.
text: Asking the assistant The application carries this manual inside it, and an assistant that has read it. Instead of looking a page up, you can ask — and for a few things, you can ask it to do the work. Two ways to open it Press F1. The assistant opens already asking about the screen you are on: on the Leads board it asks about Leads, on Marketing about Marketing, and so on. It works from anywhere — inside a list, on a button, in the side menu. Click the round button in the bottom right corner. That opens the assistant with no question: use it when what you want to know has nothing to do with where you are. Asking a question Type in the box at the bottom — "how do I export the mailing list", "what happens if I remove a user" — and press Enter. The answer comes from the pages of this manual: the assistant is told to stay inside them, to cite the page it used, and to say when it does not know rather than invent. Read more opens the whole page inside the assistant. The conversation stays as you move around the application, and the ↻ button at the top clears it. Asking it to do things Three things the assistant can do in this application, and nothing else: Ask for What happens - - "open the Marketing screen" It switches to that screen "create a lead for Mario Rossi of Zeus Red, Inc., phone 02 1234567, email mario.rossi@example.com" It creates the lead with status New and opens its detail window "prepare a proposal for Gary Orange: 12 hours of consulting at 150 each and 4 licenses at 480 each" It opens the proposal draft with the customer and the line items already in, total included It asks before it writes Anything that changes data stops and asks first, showing exactly what it is about to do: Answer No and nothing happens; the assistant is told you refused and says so. Only open the screen goes ahead without asking, because it changes nothing. It prepares, you decide Notice what the proposal action does not do: it fills the draft and leaves it open. The total is computed, the window is in front of you, and Preview and Save Proposal are still yours to press. The same with a new lead: it is created, its window opens, and correcting what the assistant understood is a normal edit. What it sends, and where The assistant uses Anthropic's Claude, so the question you type, the name of the screen you are on, the excerpts of this manual that look relevant and the outcome of any action it runs leave your machine and reach Anthropic's service. The content of your database does not: the leads, the accounts, the proposals and the attached documents stay where they are, and the assistant cannot read them. Ask it how many leads you have and it will tell you to look at the Dashboard. It needs an API key, in helpchatai.json in the HelpChatAI folder of your user profile (%APPDATA%\HelpChatAI): { "Claude": { "ApiKey": "sk-ant-..." } } Without it the assistant opens and answers that the key is missing. Everything else in the application works as always — the assistant is help, not a requirement. When it does not know If no page fits, it says so rather than inventing an answer. Two things usually help: ask with the words the application uses on screen (proposal, lead, account), and ask one thing at a time.

title: Calendar
summary: A month at a time, with today highlighted.
text: Calendar A month at a time, with today highlighted. Move between months with the two arrows at the top right of the grid, or with the arrow keys once the calendar has the focus. Saturdays and Sundays are drawn in bold, which is the one piece of behaviour the application adds to the standard control. The month and day names follow the regional settings of Windows, so on an Italian machine the heading reads ottobre 2026 and the columns dom, lun, mar…, as in the picture above. What it is not The calendar shows no data. Lead dates, proposal dates and completion dates are not marked on it, selecting a day does not filter anything, and there is no way to add an appointment. It is a month view and nothing more — see Known limitations. To see the dates of a lead, open it from the Leads board: the four dates are at the top of the detail window.

title: Dashboard
summary: The opening screen counts the leads of the active user, one tile per status.
text: Dashboard The opening screen counts the leads of the active user, one tile per status. Tile What it counts - - New Leads nobody has contacted yet Active Leads being worked on Proposal Sent Leads waiting for an answer to a proposal Closed Leads that ended, won or lost Inactive Leads parked. There is no column for them on the Leads board: this tile is the only place they are visible Total Every lead of the user, whatever the status — so it is not the sum of the five tiles above unless every lead has one of those statuses Each tile is a separate count over the Leads table filtered by the User column, so the numbers follow the user drop-down in the title bar. When the numbers change The counters are refreshed when you come back to the Dashboard, not while you work elsewhere. Move a lead on the Leads board, then click Dashboard: the new numbers are there. Leave the Dashboard open and change something from another window and the tiles will still show the old values until you leave and come back. Reading the tiles The tiles are laid out in a flow: they wrap onto a second row when the window is not wide enough for six. They are decorative — clicking a tile does nothing. To see the leads behind a number, open Leads.

title: Data model
summary: Everything is in one SQLite file, w10crmdemo.sdb, in your Documents folder, encrypted with AES-256. Five tables are stored in it; two more exist only in memory while a proposal is being drafted.
text: Data model Everything is in one SQLite file, w10crmdemo.sdb, in your Documents folder, encrypted with AES-256. Five tables are stored in it; two more exist only in memory while a proposal is being drafted. Leads The central table. One row per person you are working on. Field Type Notes LeadId auto-increment The key. Shown in the detail window and in some columns of the board Name text (100) The person Status text (100) New, Active, Proposal Sent, Closed, Inactive — free text, not a foreign key AccountName text (100) The name of the account, copied, not its id: renaming an account does not follow here OfficePhone text (100) Email text (100) Feeds the Marketing list User text (100) The owner. Every screen filters on it DateCreated date/time Stamped when the lead is created DateContacted date/time Stamped the first time it reaches Active DateDrafted date/time Stamped the first time it reaches Proposal Sent DateClosed date/time Stamped the first time it reaches Closed Notes text (2048) The three date stamps are written only if the field is still empty, so moving a lead backwards and forwards does not rewrite them. Accounts Field Type Notes AccountId auto-increment AccountName text (100) Offered in the lead's Account Name box, printed as "Bill To" Not filtered by user: the list is shared. Users Field Type Notes UserId auto-increment Username text (20) The value stored in the User column of the other tables Docs The files attached to a lead, stored whole inside the database. Field Type Notes DocId auto-increment LeadId integer Which lead it belongs to DocumentName text (20) The file name — a short limit, long names are cut Document blob The file itself User text (20) Who attached it Proposals Field Type Notes ProposalId auto-increment LeadId integer One proposal per lead is what the application enforces ProposalName text (20) Always New Proposal Status text (20) New, Accepted, Canceled Value currency The total of the invoice when it was saved Proposal blob The HTML document DateCreated date/time DateCompleted date/time Written when the proposal is accepted User text (20) While a proposal is being drafted Two tables live in memory only and are emptied each time the draft window opens. LineItems — RecordId (auto-increment), Title (text 20), Quantity (integer), Price (currency). DraftProposal — CompanyName, Address1, Address2, Phone (text 128 each), Date, Total (currency). The queries behind each screen Screen Query - - Leads, column New SELECT FROM Leads WHERE Status = 'New' AND User = :Username Leads, Active / Proposal Sent / Closed the same, with the other status Lead detail, documents SELECT FROM Docs WHERE LeadId = :LeadId AND User = :Username Sales SELECT FROM Proposals WHERE User = :Username Marketing SELECT Email, Name FROM Leads WHERE Status <> 'Inactive' AND User = :Username Accounts SELECT FROM Accounts Dashboard, one per tile SELECT COUNT(LeadId) FROM Leads WHERE Status = '…' AND User = :Username Draft, the total SELECT coalesce(sum(Quantity Price), 0) FROM LineItems Each one has a place where the Search box injects a condition, which is how filtering as you type works. The searches match with LIKE '%…%' on the upper-cased value, so they ignore case and match anywhere inside the field: Search box Looks at - - Leads name, account name, office phone, e-mail Accounts account name Sales proposal name Marketing e-mail Resetting Close the application, delete w10crmdemo.sdb, start it again: the file is rebuilt with the original sample data. There is no other way to undo anything — the application has no transaction you can roll back and no confirmation on most deletes.

title: Draft a proposal
summary: The proposal is an invoice: a header with the customer's address, a list of line items, a total, and a thank-you line. You fill it in, look at it, and save it.
text: Draft a proposal The proposal is an invoice: a header with the customer's address, a list of line items, a total, and a thank-you line. You fill it in, look at it, and save it. It opens from Create Proposal in the lead detail window, and it is modal — the rest of the application waits until you close it. A lead can have one proposal: ask for a second one and the application says This lead already has a proposal. Filling in the draft The company name is already there, taken from the lead's account, and so is today's date. The three boxes under it — street address, city/state/zip, phone — are yours to type and start out empty; they are printed as they are, and nothing is validated. The grid below is the line items: a title, a quantity and a price per row. Use the row of buttons under it to work with them: Button What it does - - + Adds an empty row − Deletes the current row ✓ Confirms the row you are editing ✗ Throws away the row you are editing ↻ Reloads the list Total recomputes itself every time a line item changes: it is the sum of quantity × price over the rows, so you never type it. The line items live in memory until you save: they belong to this draft only, and Cancel throws the whole thing away. The preview Preview turns the draft into the invoice and shows it as it will be stored. The picture above is a draft with no line items yet, which is why the table is empty and the total is $0.00. With rows in it, each one is printed as name, quantity and price. The amounts in the document are always written in the English format — $1,234.50 — whatever the regional settings of the machine are, because the document is in English. Back returns to the draft to change something; Save Proposal stores it. Saving Save Proposal writes a row in the proposals table: the generated HTML document, kept whole inside the database; the total as the value of the proposal; the status New, the creation date, and the active user; the link to the lead. Then the window closes. The proposal now shows up on the Sales page and under View Proposal in the lead. Saving does not move the lead to Proposal Sent — drag it to that column yourself when you actually send it.

title: FAQ
summary: In w10crmdemo.sdb, in your Documents folder. It is a SQLite database encrypted with AES-256, and it is the only thing the application writes — there is no settings file and no registry key.
text: FAQ Where is my data? In w10crmdemo.sdb, in your Documents folder. It is a SQLite database encrypted with AES-256, and it is the only thing the application writes — there is no settings file and no registry key. How do I start over with the sample data? Close the application, delete w10crmdemo.sdb, start it again. The file is rebuilt with the original leads, accounts and proposals. Why did all my leads disappear? Almost certainly the user drop-down in the title bar changed. Nearly every list is filtered by it. Put it back on the user that owns the records — CRMUser in the sample data. If the user itself was removed from the Users page, its records are still in the database but nothing can see them: create a user with exactly the same name and they come back. Can two people use it at the same time? No. The database is a file on your machine and the application opens it for itself. The users in the application are labels for filtering, not accounts on a server. Does the user drop-down protect anything? No. There is no password, and anybody can switch user from the title bar. It organizes work, it does not secure it. Why is the total of my proposal $0.00? Because the draft has no line items yet, or because the row you typed has not been confirmed. Press ✓ under the grid, or move to another row: the total recomputes as soon as the row is posted. Why is the amount written with a dot when my computer uses a comma? On purpose. The invoice is an English document, so its amounts are written the English way — $1,234.50 — whatever the regional settings of the machine are. What you type in the draft, and what you see in the Total box, follows your own settings. Can I change a proposal after saving it? No. The document is stored as it was generated. You can mark it Accepted or Canceled, but not edit it, and the lead cannot be given a second one. To redo a proposal, delete the existing one from the Sales list with the navigator and create a new one. Why does a lead stay in its column after I accept its proposal? Because Complete and Cancel act on the proposal, not on the lead. Moving the lead to Closed is a separate decision — drag it on the board. Which export should I use? The one on the Marketing page: it writes a delimited text file with a header row, which a spreadsheet opens directly. The exports on the Accounts and Leads pages write FireDAC's own format, meant to be read back by this application. Does the assistant need an internet connection? Yes, and an API key: it uses Anthropic's Claude. Put the key in helpchatai.json under %APPDATA%\HelpChatAI. Without it the assistant opens and says the key is missing, and the rest of the application works exactly as before — see Asking the assistant. Does my data leave the machine when I use the assistant? Your question, the name of the screen you are on, the excerpts of this manual that look relevant and the outcome of any action it runs. Not the database: leads, accounts, proposals and attached documents are never sent, and the assistant cannot read them. Can the assistant change my data? Only in the three ways listed in Asking the assistant, and the two that write something stop and ask first, showing what they are about to do. It never saves a proposal and never deletes anything. Can I attach a big file to a lead? It will work, but the file goes inside the database, so the .sdb grows by that much and every backup carries it. Also, the document name is stored in a 20-character field: longer file names are cut. Why are the icons hard to see when I change style? They are white images. They are made for a dark background: the three styles shipped with this build — SlateGray, Dark and Blue — all work. A light style would wash them out. Is this a product? No, it is a demonstration of VCL controls — the split view, the relative and card panels, the calendar view, LiveBindings over FireDAC, styles, scaling. Read Known limitations before using any of it as a starting point.

title: Getting started
summary: There is nothing to install and nothing to configure. The first time you start the application it:
text: Getting started The first run There is nothing to install and nothing to configure. The first time you start the application it: creates w10crmdemo.sdb in your Documents folder; copies the sample data into it — 8 leads, 8 accounts, one user, three proposals; encrypts the file with AES-256 and reopens it; shows the Dashboard. Every later run just opens that file. If you want the original sample data back, close the application, delete w10crmdemo.sdb and start it again. The sample data The leads are named after colours (Gary Orange, Cathy Black, James Blue, Karen Red…) and the accounts after Greek gods (Zeus Red Inc., Hera Blue Inc., Apollo Orange LLC…), so it is easy to tell at a glance which record you are looking at. They are spread over the four statuses: three New, two Active, one Proposal Sent, two Closed. The only user is CRMUser, and every sample record belongs to it. The two drop-downs in the title bar The style on the left changes the look of the whole application immediately. The choices are the ones compiled into this build: Windows10 SlateGray (the default, and the one every picture in this manual uses), Windows10 Dark and Windows10 Blue. The window is maximized when you change it. The icons of the application are white, so they only show up well on a dark style. On Windows10 Blue they are readable too; a light style would wash them out. The user on the right chooses whose records you see — see Users. Making the window smaller The layout reacts to the width: under about 640 points the navigation menu collapses to icons by itself, and opens again when you make the window wider; each section's buttons drop their captions and shrink to icons when their banner gets too narrow, so they never overlap the search box; the ☰ button collapses and expands the menu whatever the width is. The picture above is the Leads board with the menu collapsed: the four columns get the room the menu was using. Keyboard The application defines no shortcuts of its own. The usual Windows keys work: Tab moves between the controls, the arrow keys move inside the grids, F10/Alt reaches the window menu. Typing in a Search box filters as you type — there is no button to press and no Enter to confirm.

title: CRM Demo
summary: A small customer-relationship manager: it keeps the leads you are working on, the accounts they belong to, the proposals you send them, and the documents attached to each one. Everything lives in a single encrypted SQLite file on your own machine, so the application needs no server and no network.
text: CRM Demo A small customer-relationship manager: it keeps the leads you are working on, the accounts they belong to, the proposals you send them, and the documents attached to each one. Everything lives in a single encrypted SQLite file on your own machine, so the application needs no server and no network. The main window Four things are always on screen. Where What it is - - The dark strip on the left The navigation menu: Dashboard, Accounts, Leads, Sales, Marketing, Calendar, Users. The ☰ button at the top collapses it to icons The tabs along the top The same seven sections. Clicking a tab and clicking a menu entry do the same thing The banner under the tabs The name of the section, and on the right the buttons that act on it, plus a Search box The title bar Two drop-downs: the visual style of the application, and the active user The window remembers nothing between runs: it opens maximized on the Dashboard. The active user is a filter, not a login The drop-down on the right of the title bar chooses who you are working as. It is not a login — there is no password — but it filters nearly everything: the leads, the proposals, the documents and the marketing e-mails you see are only those whose User field matches the name selected there, and the Dashboard counters are counted the same way. Change it and the lists change under you. Any detail window that was open is closed first. Where your data is On the first run the application creates w10crmdemo.sdb in your Documents folder, fills it with the sample data this manual uses, and encrypts it with AES-256. From then on it opens that file. Delete it and the next run builds a fresh one with the original sample data — which is the simplest way to start over. See Data model for what is inside it. Asking instead of reading Press F1 anywhere, or click the round button in the bottom right corner. The assistant answers from these pages, and it can also do three things for you — open a screen, create a lead, prepare a proposal — asking first whenever it is about to write something. See Asking the assistant. Where to go next Index — every page of this manual Asking the assistant — the help built into the application Leads — the board where the work actually happens Lead detail — one lead, its documents and its proposal FAQ — the questions that come up first

title: Lead detail
summary: Everything about one lead: who it is, where it stands, the documents attached to it and the proposal sent to it.
text: Lead detail Everything about one lead: who it is, where it stands, the documents attached to it and the proposal sent to it. It opens from the Leads board, by double-clicking a row or pressing View Lead. The window is not modal: you can leave it open and keep moving around the board, and it follows the selection. The fields Field Notes - - Lead Id Assigned by the database, shown for reference only Status The five statuses, picked from a list. Changing it here moves the lead to another column of the board, exactly like dragging it — except that no date is stamped Date Created / Contacted / Drafted / Closed The four stages. An empty date shows an empty box; pick one from the calendar to fill it, and it stays until you change it Name The person Account Name Picked from the accounts. The proposal prints this name as "Bill To" Office Phone, Email Free text, not validated User Who the lead belongs to. It follows the active user and is not meant to be edited here Notes Free text, up to 2048 characters Every field is written to the database as soon as you leave it — there is no Save button and no Cancel. Closing the window keeps what you typed. The Call and Email buttons beside the phone and the e-mail do nothing: they are placeholders. See Known limitations. Documents The panel on the right holds the files attached to this lead. They are stored inside the database, not referenced on disk, so the attachment travels with the .sdb file. Add Document asks for a file and loads it whole into the database, keeping the file name and recording who attached it. View Document writes the selected document to your temporary folder and opens it with whatever program Windows associates with that extension. If no document is selected it says so. Delete Document asks for confirmation, naming the document, and then removes it. The list shows the id and the document name; it is filtered by lead and by the active user. The four buttons in the banner At the top right, left to right: Button What it does - - Complete Proposal Marks this lead's proposal as Accepted and stamps its completion date Cancel Proposal Marks it as Canceled. The proposal stays in the database View Proposal Opens the saved proposal — see Sales Create Proposal Opens the draft window. One proposal per lead: if there already is one, it tells you so and does nothing When the window is narrow the four buttons lose their captions and stay as icons, in that same order. Note that Complete and Cancel act on the proposal, not on the lead: neither of them moves the lead to Closed. Moving it is up to you, on the board.

title: Leads
summary: The board where the work happens: four columns, one per status, and a lead moves from left to right as it progresses.
text: Leads The board where the work happens: four columns, one per status, and a lead moves from left to right as it progresses. Column Meaning Columns shown New Nobody has called yet Date Created, Name Active Being worked on Date Contacted, Name, Email, Office Phone, Lead Id Proposal Sent A proposal is out, waiting for an answer Date Drafted, Account Name Closed Finished Date Closed, Account Name Each column shows the date that matters at that stage, which is why the first column is different in each one. A fifth status, Inactive, exists in the data but has no column here: those leads are only counted on the Dashboard. Moving a lead: drag and drop Drag a row from one column and drop it on another. Two things happen: the lead takes the status of the column you dropped it on; if the date of that stage is still empty, it is stamped with now — Date Contacted moving to Active, Date Drafted moving to Proposal Sent, Date Closed moving to Closed. A date that already has a value is left alone, so moving a lead back and forth does not rewrite its history. Dropping a lead on the column it already is in does nothing. The four lists refresh after every move, and the lead you dragged stays selected. Opening a lead Double-click a row, or select it and press View Lead. Either one opens the lead detail window on that lead. Simply moving the selection in a column is enough to make that lead the current one — the detail window, if it is open, follows the selection, and the navigator at the bottom of the page starts acting on the column you clicked last. Create Lead Create Lead makes a new lead straight away, with no questions asked: status New, so it appears at the bottom of the first column; name First Last, a placeholder you are meant to replace; the active user, and Date Created set to now. The detail window opens on it immediately so you can fill it in. Search The Search box filters all four columns at once, as you type. It matches, ignoring case and anywhere inside the value, against the lead's name, account name, office phone or e-mail — so typing black finds Cathy Black, and typing example.com finds everybody. Clear the box to get the full board back. Export Leads Export Leads writes the whole Leads table to a file you choose, in FireDAC's own format (the extension decides between binary, XML and JSON). It is a backup you can read back with the same application, not a spreadsheet. The navigator at the bottom The arrows move through the column you last clicked in; − deletes the current lead and ↻ reloads the list. There is no confirmation on the delete.

title: Marketing
summary: The mailing list: the e-mail address and the name of every lead of the active user that is not Inactive.
text: Marketing The mailing list: the e-mail address and the name of every lead of the active user that is not Inactive. The list is built from the leads, not stored separately, so it is always up to date: change a lead's e-mail and it changes here; park a lead as Inactive and it drops out. Leads without an address appear with an empty e-mail — nothing filters them out. The list is read-only: there is no navigator under it and nothing to edit. Fix an address in the lead detail window. Search The Search box filters as you type, on the e-mail address (not the name), ignoring case and matching anywhere — example.com keeps everybody, karen finds one. Export Export writes the list to a delimited text file with a header row of field names: the one export in the application that a spreadsheet or a mailing tool can read directly. It writes what the query returns — so the current search filter does apply, unlike the exports on the Accounts and Leads pages, which always write the whole table. Choose the file name in the dialog; the application overwrites it without asking. The application writes a Data.log next to the exported file, a log of the copy. It is harmless and can be deleted.

title: Sales
summary: Every proposal of the active user, in one list.
text: Sales Every proposal of the active user, in one list. Column Meaning - - ProposalId Assigned by the database LeadId The lead the proposal was written for ProposalName Always New Proposal: the draft window does not ask for a name Status New when saved, then Accepted or Canceled Value The total of the invoice, as it was when you saved it Proposal The document itself. The grid cannot show it and prints (OBJECT) DateCreated, DateCompleted When it was saved, and when it was accepted User Who wrote it Complete and Cancel The two buttons in the banner act on the selected proposal: Complete sets the status to Accepted and stamps DateCompleted with now; Cancel sets the status to Canceled and leaves the completion date alone. Neither asks for confirmation, and both can be applied again later — nothing is locked once a proposal is accepted. If the list is empty the buttons do nothing. The same two actions are on the lead detail window, where they apply to that lead's proposal. Search The Search box filters as you type, on the proposal name only — which, since every proposal is called New Proposal, is not as useful as it sounds. To find the proposal of a given customer, open the lead and press View Proposal. Reading a proposal View Proposal in the lead detail opens the document stored in the database, exactly as it was saved. The window has two buttons: Close, and Complete, which does the same thing as Complete here — marks the proposal accepted and closes the window.

title: Known limitations
summary: What this demonstration does not do, and what to watch out for. The list comes from reading the source, not from guessing.
text: Known limitations What this demonstration does not do, and what to watch out for. The list comes from reading the source, not from guessing. Not implemented Where What - - The assistant Three actions only: open a screen, create a lead, prepare a proposal. It cannot move a lead between columns, create an account, save a proposal or delete anything Lead detail The Call and Email buttons next to the phone number and the address have no action behind them Calendar The month view is not bound to anything: no lead date is marked on it, selecting a day filters nothing, appointments cannot be added Sales Every proposal is called New Proposal — the draft window never asks for a name — which makes the search box on this page nearly useless Sales The document column of the list shows (OBJECT), because a grid cannot render the stored HTML Proposals A saved proposal cannot be edited or reprinted, only accepted or cancelled Easy to get wrong Remove asks nothing. Removing an account, a user or a row from a navigator happens immediately and cannot be undone. Only Delete Document asks for confirmation. Removing a user hides its records instead of reassigning or deleting them. They reappear if a user with the same name is created again. Accounts are copied by name into a lead, not referenced: renaming or deleting an account leaves the lead pointing at a name that no longer exists. Nothing is validated: an account with an empty name, two accounts with the same name, an e-mail that is not an e-mail, a quantity of zero — all accepted. The sample data itself contains an account with an empty name and id 0. Accepting a proposal does not close its lead, and nothing stops a proposal from being accepted and then cancelled. Field sizes worth knowing DocumentName, ProposalName, Status and the line item Title are 20 characters, and Username is 20 too. Longer values are cut when stored. The lead's own fields are 100, and the notes 2048. Security The database is encrypted with AES-256, but the password is written in the source code (DB_PASSWORD in uDataMod.pas). That is fine for a demonstration and worth nothing in a real application: anyone with the executable has the key. There is no login, and the user drop-down protects nothing. Technical notes for whoever reads the code These were found and fixed while preparing this manual, and are worth knowing if you compare the code with the original Embarcadero version: the total of a draft was computed with SQL printf("%.2f", …), which returns a string with a dot, and then read as a currency: on a machine with Italian regional settings that raised '0.00' is not a valid floating point value. The query now returns a number; the generated invoice took its amounts from the screen and from AsString, so an Italian machine produced $1.800,00 in an English document. They now go through an explicit en-US format; AddInvoiceData declared its parameters as (AName, APrice, AQuantity) but was called with (Title, Quantity, Price): the output was right only because the two mistakes cancelled out; two resize handlers multiplied a size that was already in screen pixels by ScaleFactor, which at 150% or 175% made a grid column wider than its grid; two width comparisons (640 and 936) were raw constants, so the layout switched at the wrong size on a scaled display; the column widths of the bound grids are stored in design pixels and LiveBindings reapplies them after the VCL has scaled the grid, so at 175% the columns stayed narrow and cut the text. They are now scaled once at start-up. Still open in the code: five in-memory tables are freed while they are still components of the data module; the drag-and-drop handler repeats the same block four times and can call Locate with -1; a temporary file written by View Document is never deleted; and the two proposal windows use the legacy Internet Explorer control to display their HTML.

title: Users
summary: The names records can belong to. The sample database has one, CRMUser, and everything in it belongs to that user.
text: Users The names records can belong to. The sample database has one, CRMUser, and everything in it belongs to that user. What a user is here Not an account you log into — there is no password and no permission. A user is a label on a record and a filter on what you see. The drop-down at the right of the title bar picks the active one, and from that moment: the Leads board, the Sales list, the documents of a lead and the Marketing list show only the records whose User matches; the Dashboard counters count only those; anything you create — a lead, a proposal, a document — is stamped with that name. Accounts are the exception: they are shared by everybody. Switching user closes the lead, draft and proposal windows that are open, so you never keep looking at a record that the new filter has hidden. Create Create asks for the name, starting from user. It is the one place in the application that checks for duplicates: a name already in the list is refused with A user with that username already exists. The new user starts with nothing — an empty board, zeros on the dashboard. To give it something to work on, switch to it and create a lead, or change the User of an existing one. Remove Remove deletes the selected user immediately, without asking. Nothing checks whether that user owns anything. The leads, proposals and documents stamped with that name stay in the database but stop being visible, because no user in the drop-down matches them any more. Removing the only user leaves an application that shows nothing at all. If it happens, the way back is to create a user with exactly the same name as before: the records are keyed by the name, so they reappear.
